source: make a 1+ speed obby with 10 levels and every level get more harder the further you go and there are treadmills you can run on to get more speed

answers.ask: No theme was stated - should the ten levels share one look, or change theme as they get harder?
answers.answer: Use one consistent simple cartoon obby look across all ten levels so the build stays clear and focused on the increasing difficulty.

answers.ask: Should the ten levels run along the ground or stack into a tower?
answers.answer: Stack the ten levels into a tower, with each higher level being harder than the last.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: No theme was stated - should the ten levels share one look, or change theme as they get harder? A: Use one consistent simple cartoon obby look across all ten levels so the build stays clear and focused on the increasing difficulty.
- [author] shape — Q: Should the ten levels run along the ground or stack into a tower? A: Stack the ten levels into a tower, with each higher level being harder than the last.
- [agent_inferred] training_distribution — Q: Where should the treadmills be placed across the ten levels? A: Put one treadmill training station at the start of each level, for exactly 10 treadmills.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a simple cartoon speed-training obby built as a tower of exactly 10 stacked levels. Give every level one clearly marked treadmill at its start, followed by an ordered platform route, and make each higher level visibly harder than the one below through progressively more demanding platform spacing and arrangement. Separate successive levels with clear physical thresholds so the upward progression is easy to read. Add a safe recovery pad at the start of every level and one obvious reward area at the top after level 10. Keep one consistent uncluttered cartoon palette across the full tower and frame all 10 layers clearly.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation, canonical slug `simulation`, because raising the speed stat on treadmills is the progression loop. Obby & Platformer, canonical slug `obby-platformer`, is secondary because each of the 10 tiers is also a physical platform challenge.

## Shape and preset
Use `course-tower`, Path (Tower / Spiral Ascent), from outside Simulation's usual shapes because the author explicitly confirmed 10 vertically stacked levels with surfaces overhanging those below. The matched preset is Stat Grinder, with its ordinary tier-ladder shape replaced by the confirmed tower and with unrequested shop and rebirth areas omitted.

## Config requirements
Use `station-training` for exactly 10 visible treadmills, one at the start of each level. Use `gate-progression` for the clear threshold between each speed tier, `path-track` for the ordered platform route through every level, and `obstacle-jump` for progressively harder platform arrangements. Use the visible halves of `checkpoint-respawn` for safe level-start pads and `winner-zone` for the top reward area.

## Layout requirements
Place exactly 10 `station-training` TriggerZones, one on each level's treadmill. Place exactly 10 `checkpoint-respawn` Checkpoints on safe pads at the start of levels 1–10. Place nine progression gates between successive levels, each after the preceding route and before the next treadmill. Place one `winner-zone` WinnerZone after level 10 at the top.

## Layout components
The build contains one 10-level stacked tower, exactly 10 treadmills, 10 safe start pads, nine inter-level thresholds, 10 ordered platform sections of increasing difficulty, vertical connections between levels, and one top reward zone. Open air around the tower forms the failure boundary. Compose all layers so their order from level 1 through level 10 is unmistakable.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: draw one authoritative plan for each stacked level and validate the ordered connections before dressing the tower isometrically. The top-down level plans are authoritative because broken transitions or impossible platform spacing would make progression fail, while this non-maze, non-racing tower does not support `authored_plan`.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale is large, driven by 10 stacked playable levels while retaining individual treadmills, gates, and platforms. The theme is a consistent simple cartoon obby. Use `P6` because every platform chain and level transition must be valid by construction, and `P2` because the 10 tower levels overhang and occlude one another.
